profile_notes: Scoped to living subjects in the field (animals/birds), NOT landscape. GATE: require:[] deliberately. Body-level specs (fps_electronic, af_low_light_ev, resolution_mp, iso_native, sensor_format) are sparsely populated across the corpus (task-stated ~6-8/48 bodies); a hard spec gate here would empty the guide, so fit is expressed entirely through axis weights, which every card carries. CRUX TRIO at 3: autofocus_body (subject/eye detection + tracking is the single most-cited wildlife differentiator; animal-eye AF is standard since ~2023 and drives keeper rate on erratic subjects), af_performance (real-world AF acquisition speed/hit-rate on distant, fast subjects), and burst_buffer (frame rate + buffer depth for birds-in-flight and action bursts). AF is intentionally represented on TWO axes (autofocus_body + af_performance) so it carries more total weight than burst, matching the research consensus that AF is of 'utmost importance' while burst is critical-but-secondary. SECONDARY: sensor_performance=2 (high-ISO / low-light headroom for dawn-dusk animal activity, fast shutter speeds, and cropping distant subjects), build=2 (weather sealing / field durability). SUPPORTING at 1: stabilization (handheld long-lens work; note IBIS often co-works with lens IS), handling (long field sessions, big-lens balance), evf_lcd (tracking moving subjects; low-blackout finder), battery_life (long field days). Deliberately UNWEIGHTED (0/omitted): video_capability, connectivity, image_quality, color_rendition — real but not what separates wildlife-capable bodies. gear_class excludes novelty only. NATURE-SCOPE JUDGMENT: 'nature' is kept in the lexicon as a wildlife co-occurrence term, but generic 'nature photography' / landscape queries are intentionally NOT in query_aliases because landscape needs (resolution, dynamic range, wide lenses, tripod) invert this profile's weighting; landscape should be a separate sibling profile if demand warrants.
